title: NTA UGC NET English Full Mock Test #04
subtitle: 100 Questions · 200 Marks · Post-2018 NTA Pattern · Zero Answer Bias (25 A/B/C/D) · Reading Comprehension (Q91-100)

items.title: Mock #04 · Q1
items.stem:
Match the following :
(Novel) — (Setting)
I. The Power and the Glory — 1. Vietnam
II. The Quiet American — 2. Haiti
III. The Honorary Consul — 3. Paraguay
IV. The Comedians — 4. Mexico
The right combination according to the code is :
Code : I II III IV
items.explanation: Graham Greene's novels match with their settings as follows: The Power and the Glory is set in Mexico (I-4), The Quiet American in Vietnam (II-1), The Honorary Consul on the Argentine border with Paraguay (III-3), and The Comedians in Papa Doc Duvalier's Haiti (IV-2).

items.title: Mock #04 · Q2
items.stem: Which of the following is true of The Canterbury Tales ?
options: Chaucer, the pilgrim, narrates Sir Thopas' Tale only
Chaucer, the pilgrim, narrates The Tale of Melibee only
Chaucer, the pilgrim does attempt to narrate an unnamed tale but abruptly stops due to the intervention of the other pilgrims
Chaucer, the pilgrim, narrates both Sir Thopas' Tale and The Tale of Melibee
items.explanation: In Fragment VII of Geoffrey Chaucer's The Canterbury Tales, Chaucer's pilgrim persona first narrates the burlesque tail-rhyme romance 'The Tale of Sir Thopas' until the Host Harry Bailly interrupts his 'drasty rymyng', whereupon Chaucer narrates the long moral prose treatise 'The Tale of Melibee'.

items.title: Mock #04 · Q3
items.stem:
Which two of the following words are borrowed into English from Czech?
(A) pistol
(B) robot
(C) sauna
(D) coach
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
items.explanation: 'Pistol' (from Czech pišťala) and 'robot' (from Czech robota) came into English from Czech. Sauna is Finnish and coach is Hungarian.

items.title: Mock #04 · Q4
items.stem: What is an “implied reader” ?
options: The ideal audience envisioned by the author and to whom the work of literature is supposedly addressed.
The ideal “average” reader who can approach a work of literature with no preconceived ideas about the author’s life, the time of composition, etc.
A reader who embodies all those predispositions necessary for a literary work to exercise its effect.
The ideal reader of a work of literature which is approximated over time by successive responses of generations of actual readers.
items.explanation: Wolfgang Iser's implied reader is the role built into the text, embodying the predispositions needed for the work to have its effect.

items.title: Mock #04 · Q5
items.stem:
What is the correct chronological sequence of the following Dalit Women Writers in order of the birth?
A. Urmila Pawar
B. Bama
C. Meena Kandasamy
D. Gogu Shyamala
E. Kumud Pawde
items.explanation: Arranged by birth year: Marathi Sanskritist Kumud Pawde was born in 1938 (E), Marathi autobiographer Urmila Pawar in 1945 (A), Tamil novelist Bama in 1958 (B), Telugu writer Gogu Shyamala in 1969 (D), and poet Meena Kandasamy in 1984 (C). This establishes the order E, A, B, D, C.

items.title: Mock #04 · Q6
items.stem: F. Turner's famous hypothesis is that
options: the Frontier has outlived its ideological utility in American civilization.
the Frontier has posed a challenge to the American creative imagination.
the Frontier has been the one great determinant of American civilization.
the Frontier has been the one great deterrent to American progress.
items.explanation: In his landmark 1893 address 'The Significance of the Frontier in American History,' historian Frederick Jackson Turner propounded the 'Frontier Thesis,' arguing that the moving western frontier was the primary determinant of American democracy, character, and civilization.

items.title: Mock #04 · Q7
items.meta: Unit IX: Literary Theory Post World War II
items.stem:
Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A) : To give a text an author is to impose a limit on that text, to furnish it with a final signified, to close the writing.

Reason (R) : A text is made up of multiple meanings drawn from many sources, and this multiplicity is focused on the reader.

In the context of the two statements, which one of the following is correct :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
items.explanation: Drawn directly from Roland Barthes's 1967 essay 'The Death of the Author,' both statements are true and (R) explains why assigning an Author-God limits a text whose tissue of quotations actually finds its unity in the reader (A).

items.title: Mock #04 · Q8
items.stem:
Which of the following statements on
Pathetic Fallacy is NOT TRUE ?
options: This term applies to descriptions that are not true but imaginary and fanciful
The term was originally used by Alexander Pope in his Pastorals
In its first use, the term was used with disapproval because nature cannot be equated with the human in respect of emotions and responses
Pathetic Fallacy is generally understood as human traits being applied or attributed to non-human things in nature
items.explanation: The critical term 'pathetic fallacy'—meaning the attribution of human emotions and traits to inanimate nature—was coined not by Alexander Pope, but by the Victorian critic John Ruskin in Volume III of Modern Painters (1856).

items.title: Mock #04 · Q9
items.stem:
Which of the following works of Browning are pure dramas?
A. Strafford
B. The Last Ride Together
C. A Blot in the 'Scutcheon
D. Pippa Passes
E. Porphyria's Lover
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Strafford (1837, A) and A Blot in the 'Scutcheon (1843, C) are full-length stage tragedies ('pure dramas') written by Robert Browning, whereas 'The Last Ride Together' and 'Porphyria's Lover' are dramatic monologues and Pippa Passes is a verse closet drama of linked scenes.

items.title: Mock #04 · Q10
items.stem:
Which one of Joseph Conrad's novels expresses the contrast between the solidarity of
shipboard life and the profound underlying loneliness of existence thus : "loneliness
impenetrable and transparent, elusive and everlasting…. that surrounds, envelops, clothes
every human soul from the cradle to the grave, and perhaps beyond" ?
items.explanation: In Joseph Conrad's maritime fiction, most notably Lord Jim (1900), Conrad contrasts the moral bond and shared solidarity of shipboard life with the 'loneliness impenetrable and transparent, elusive and everlasting... that surrounds, envelops, clothes every human soul from the cradle to the grave, and perhaps beyond'.

items.title: Mock #04 · Q11
items.stem:
Match List I with List II:
List I
A. Some are born great, others achieve greatness.
B. Love looks not with the eyes, but with the mind, / And therefore is winged Cupid painted blind.
C. Ill deeds is doubled with an evil word.
D. We are such stuff as dreams are made on, and our little life is rounded with a sleep.

List II
I. The Tempest
II. The Comedy of Errors
III. A Midsummer Night's Dream
IV. Twelfth Night

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: In William Shakespeare's plays: Malvolio reads 'Some are born great...' in Twelfth Night (II.v, A-IV); Helena speaks 'Love looks not with the eyes...' in A Midsummer Night's Dream (I.i, B-III); Luciana says 'A sin of ill deeds is doubled with an evil word' in The Comedy of Errors (III.ii, C-II); and Prospero speaks 'We are such stuff as dreams are made on...' in The Tempest (IV.i, D-I).

items.title: Mock #04 · Q12
items.stem:
Being so caught up, so mastered by the brute __________ of the air, Did she put on his
knowledge with his power, Before the __________ beak could let her drop.
Yeats, “Leda and the Swan”.
Choose the right words for the blanks :
items.explanation: In W. B. Yeats's sonnet 'Leda and the Swan' (1923), the octave and sestet pivot on the lines: 'Being so caught up, so mastered by the brute blood of the air, / Did she put on his knowledge with his power / Before the indifferent beak could let her drop?'

items.title: Mock #04 · Q13
items.stem:
Which two of the following are Samuel Johnson’s statements about metaphysical poets?
(A) they were singular in their thoughts
(B) they were careful in their diction
(C) they effected combination of dissimilar images
(D) they avoided occult resemblances
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
items.explanation: In the Life of Cowley, Johnson says the metaphysicals were singular in thought and yoked together dissimilar images. He says they discovered, not avoided, occult resemblances.

items.title: Mock #04 · Q14
items.stem: Which among the following does not belong to Indo-European language family ?
items.explanation: Finnish belongs to the Finno-Ugric branch of the Uralic language family, whereas English, German, and the Scandinavian languages all belong to the Germanic branch of the Indo-European language family.

items.title: Mock #04 · Q15
items.stem:
What is the correct chronological order of the following poets ?
(A) Thomas Carew
(B) Edward Herbert
(C) John Donne
(D) George Herbert
(E) James Shirley
items.explanation: The chronological order of these early modern poets by birth is John Donne (1572–1631), Edward Herbert, Lord Herbert of Cherbury (1583–1648), George Herbert (1593–1633), Thomas Carew (1595–1640), and James Shirley (1596–1666).

items.title: Mock #04 · Q16
items.stem: Which of the following book by V.S. Naipaul is subtitled The Caribbean Revisited ?
items.explanation: V. S. Naipaul's first travel book, The Middle Passage (1962), recording his return journey through five colonial societies in the West Indies and South America, was republished with the subtitle The Caribbean Revisited.

items.title: Mock #04 · Q17
items.stem:
Given below are two statements : One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion (A): Jacques Lacan was radically critical of the existing psychoanalytical theory.
Reason (R): Lacan was expelled from the International Psychoanalytical Association in 1959.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
items.explanation: Jacques Lacan critiqued ego psychology and existing orthodox psychoanalytic theory through his structuralist 'return to Freud' (Assertion A is true), but he left/was excluded from the IPA during the 1953 split and the 1963 'excommunication,' not in 1959 (Reason R is false).

items.title: Mock #04 · Q18
items.stem:
Samuel Johnson denounced the metaphysical poets saying, "About the beginning of the
seventeenth century appeared a race of writers that may be termed the metaphysical poets".
In the biography of which of the following poets in his Lives of Poets did Johnson make this
remark ?
items.explanation: Samuel Johnson coined and critiqued the term 'metaphysical poets'—describing their discordia concors as heterogeneous ideas yoked by violence together—in his 'Life of Cowley' from Lives of the Most Eminent English Poets (1779–1781).

items.title: Mock #04 · Q19
items.stem:
Which two aspects of cultural diffusion in the Age of Globalization need to be addressed by pedagogy of language in general and of English in particular?
(a) Unidirectionality
(b) Multidirectionality
(c) Complex and extensive
(d) Simplistic and abbreviated
Choose the correct option :
items.explanation: In the age of globalization, cultural and linguistic flows operate across multiple global centers simultaneously. Language pedagogy therefore needs to address the multidirectionality (b) and the complex and extensive nature (c) of cultural diffusion.

items.title: Mock #04 · Q20
items.stem:
Which of the following statements is true of the working group set up by the University Grants Commission in 1978 to
study the medium of instruction in higher education?
options: It observed that English need not be displaced as the medium of instruction although regional languages were quite ready to take over its functions
It recommended a quicker switchover of the medium of instruction from English to Indian languages
It argued that English as a highly developed language was best suited for India's industrial and scientific progress
It asserted that English had the potential to further polarize an already-divided nation along socio-economic and intellectual fault lines
items.explanation: The 1978 University Grants Commission (UGC) working group on the medium of instruction observed that English need not be hastily displaced in higher education, even as regional Indian languages developed capacity to assume academic functions.

items.title: Mock #04 · Q21
items.stem:
Match List I with List II:
List I (Author):
A. Humayun Kabir
B. Bhabani Bhattacharya
C. Manohar Malgonkar
D. Kamala Markandaya

List II (Novel):
I. A Goddess Named Gold
II. Men and Rivers
III. Combat of Shadows
IV. Possession

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Humayun Kabir wrote Men and Rivers (1945, A-II), Bhabani Bhattacharya wrote A Goddess Named Gold (1960, B-I), Manohar Malgonkar wrote Combat of Shadows (1962, C-III), and Kamala Markandaya wrote Possession (1963, D-IV), giving A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV.

items.title: Mock #04 · Q22
items.stem: Why do the Houyhnhnms have so few words in their language ?
options: They consider language to be morally corrupt and prefer to remain silent
Their wants and passions are fewer than human wants and passions, and they need fewer words
They find speech difficult because they are horses
items.explanation: In Part IV, Chapter 4 of Jonathan Swift's Gulliver's Travels (1726), Gulliver explains that the rational horse-like Houyhnhnms have a very small vocabulary because their wants and passions are fewer than those of humans, and their wholly virtuous society has no words for lying, power, war, punishment, or evil.

items.title: Mock #04 · Q23
items.stem:
Which two of the following poems by Seamus Heaney come under his Bog Poems?
(A) “Personal Helicon”
(B) “Punishment”
(C) “The Early Purges”
(D) “Tollund Man”
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
items.explanation: 'Punishment' and 'The Tollund Man' are Heaney's bog poems, about preserved Iron Age bodies.

items.title: Mock #04 · Q24
items.stem:
Who among the following theorists holds that metaphor and metonymy are the two
fundamental structures of language ?
items.explanation: In his landmark 1956 essay 'Two Aspects of Language and Two Types of Aphasic Disturbances', Russian-American linguist Roman Jakobson argued that language operates along two fundamental axes: metaphor (based on similarity and selection) and metonymy (based on contiguity and combination).

items.title: Mock #04 · Q25
items.stem: Arrange the following in the chronological order of publication
options: Memoriam - A Christmas Carol - Men and Women - Henry Esmond
Christmas Carol - In Memoriam - Men and Women - Henry Esmond
Memoriam - A Christmas Carol - Henry Esmond - Men and Women
Christmas Carol - In Memoriam - Henry Esmond - Men and Women
items.explanation: The correct chronological sequence of these Victorian works is: Charles Dickens's A Christmas Carol (1843), Alfred, Lord Tennyson's In Memoriam A.H.H. (1850), William Makepeace Thackeray's The History of Henry Esmond (1852), and Robert Browning's Men and Women (1855).

items.title: Mock #04 · Q26
items.stem: How the words from a language other than English are written in a research paper?
items.explanation: In academic style guides including the MLA Handbook, words and phrases from a language other than English that have not been naturalized into English are formatted in italics.

items.title: Mock #04 · Q27
items.stem:
Given below are two statements. One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion (A): Co-operative learning activities are those in which students must work together in order to complete a task or solve a problem.
Reason (R): These techniques are used to identify a weak learner and to separate him/her from the rest of the members of the group for taking special care of him/her.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the option given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
items.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct because cooperative learning requires students to collaborate in small groups to complete tasks or solve problems, but Reason (R) is false because cooperative learning integrates learners of diverse abilities rather than isolating or separating weak learners from the group.

items.title: Mock #04 · Q28
items.stem:
"It blurs distinctions among literary,
non-literary and cultural texts, showing
how all three intercirculate, share in, and
mutually constitute each other." What
does it in this statement stand for ?
items.explanation: Pioneered by Stephen Greenblatt in the 1980s, New Historicism rejects the formalist autonomy of the literary text, reading literary works alongside non-literary and cultural documents to show how all three intercirculate and mutually construct historical power and meaning.

items.title: Mock #04 · Q29
items.stem: Which among the following are not mentioned as the aspects of the novel by E.M. Forster? (A) Story (B) Imagination (C) Plot (D) Harmony (E) Prophecy Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: In Aspects of the Novel (1927), E.M. Forster lists seven specific aspects of the novel: The Story, People, The Plot, Fantasy, Prophecy, Pattern, and Rhythm. Neither 'Imagination' (B) nor 'Harmony' (D) is included among Forster's seven aspects.

items.title: Mock #04 · Q30
items.stem: Who among the following is NOT an Australian writer ?
items.explanation: Bill Pearson (1922–2002), author of the realist novel Coal Flat (1963) and the essay 'Fretful Sleepers,' was a New Zealand writer and scholar. Morris West, Patrick White, and Thomas Keneally are all prominent Australian novelists.

items.title: Mock #04 · Q31
items.stem:
Match List I with List Il

feisty ist
Author 'Text

lA. Thomas Pynchon LG.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below
items.explanation: American postmodernist Thomas Pynchon published his debut novel V. in 1963 (A-II), and British novelist Howard Jacobson wrote the dystopian novel J (2014, B-III). Anthony Burgess authored the structuralist-inspired novel M/F (1971, C-IV), and art critic John Berger won the 1972 Booker Prize for his novel G. (D-I).

items.title: Mock #04 · Q32
items.stem: Who among the following refers to Byron’s works as “monstrous combinations of horrors and mockery, lewdness and impiety”?
items.explanation: Robert Southey fiercely attacked Lord Byron in the Preface to his poem A Vision of Judgement (1821), condemning Byron's writings as "monstrous combinations of horrors and mockery, lewdness and impiety" and branding Byron and Shelley as leaders of the "Satanic School."

items.title: Mock #04 · Q33
items.stem:
Which among the following statements do not relate to Wiliam Empson's Seven Types of Ambiguity?

'A Empson uses the term 'ambiguity' to refer to any verbal nuance which may give room for alternative reaction to the same piece of literature

B. The first type of ambiguity is simple metaphor which may be effective in several ways at once

C. The third type of ambiguity consists of tyo apparently disconnected meanings given simultaneously

. Empson calls the fifth type of ambiguity as 'unfortunate confusion' with examples from Shelley and Swinburne

E. Seventh type of ambiguity refers to the division in the reader's mind

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
items.explanation: Statements D and E do not relate: in William Empson's Seven Types of Ambiguity (1930), 'unfortunate confusion' refers to the second type rather than the fifth, and the seventh type marks a fundamental division and contradiction in the author's own mind rather than the reader's. Statements A, B, and C accurately outline Empson's definitions and earlier types of ambiguity.

items.title: Mock #04 · Q34
items.stem: How does Christ respond to the Grand Inquisitor’s accusations in Brothers Karamazov?
options: He kneels before the Grand Inquisitor
He begins to weep in remorse
He kisses the Grand Inquisitor on his lips
He says, “Mea culpa, mea culpa, mea maxima culpa”
items.explanation: Christ says nothing and gently kisses the old Inquisitor on his lips. The Inquisitor then lets him go.

items.title: Mock #04 · Q35
items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a punishment given by God to Adam and Eve as a consequence of tasting the forbidden fruit?
options: ‘Cursed is the ground for thy sake, thou in sorrow / Shalt eat thereof all the days of thy life’
‘Dust shalt eat all the days of life’
items.explanation: In the Book of Genesis (3:14) and Book X of John Milton's Paradise Lost, the curse "Dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life" is delivered directly to the serpent (Satan), whereas Eve is cursed with pain in childbirth and Adam with sorrowful labor before their expulsion from Eden.

items.title: Mock #04 · Q36
items.meta: Unit IX: Literary Theory Post World War II
items.stem: Given below are two statements: Statement (I): A Room of One's Own is a feminist essay about women's education, exclusion and writing by Virginia Woolf. Statement (II): In Other Worlds is a collection of essays written by Edward W. Said on contemporary ideas such as psychoanalysis and social theory. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are true
Statement (I) is true but Statement (II) is false
Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are false
Statement (I) is false but Statement (II) is true
items.explanation: Statement (I) is true because Virginia Woolf's A Room of One's Own (1929) is a classic feminist essay examining women's education, financial independence, and literary tradition. Statement (II) is false because In Other Worlds: Essays in Cultural Politics (1987) was written by Gayatri Chakravorty Spivak, not Edward Said.

items.title: Mock #04 · Q37
items.stem:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Wordsworth's "Intimations of Immortality from Recollections of Early Childhood" was published in 1807.
Statement II: In "Intimations of Immortality from Recollections of Early Childhood," Wordsworth sums up his philosophy of childhood.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
items.explanation: Both statements are true: William Wordsworth's 'Ode: Intimations of Immortality from Recollections of Early Childhood' was published in Poems, in Two Volumes (1807) and encapsulates his Romantic philosophy of the child's pre-existent spiritual bond with nature and the divine.

items.title: Mock #04 · Q38
items.stem:
These beauteous forms,
Through a long absence, have been to me
As is a landscape to a blind man’s eye...
(“Tintern Abbey Lines”)
Which of the following rhetorical terms best suits these lines ?
items.explanation: In 'Lines Composed a Few Miles above Tintern Abbey' (1798), William Wordsworth uses litotes (ironic understatement through double negative) in asserting that the Wye valley forms 'have not been to me / As is a landscape to a blind man's eye'.

items.title: Mock #04 · Q39
items.stem:
Which of the following observations are true about Roland Barthes' contributions to literary theory?
A. He rejected the model for structural analysis of narratives
B. He perceived "meaning" as an effect of various interconnections among linguistic codes
C. He identified the various codes found in the process of structuration
D. He played a significant role in the development of 'semiology'
E. He questioned the concept of literary criticism as an act of uncovering some hidden truth intended by the "Author"
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: B, C, D and E only
A, B, C, D and E only
items.explanation: Roland Barthes pioneered semiology (D), analyzed narrative codes in S/Z (B, C), and challenged authorial intentionality in 'The Death of the Author' (E); statement A is false because he championed structural narrative analysis in 1966, making Option 3 (B, C, D and E only) correct.

items.title: Mock #04 · Q40
items.stem: Who said “The introduction of foreigners does not necessarily destroy the nation, they merge in it”?
items.explanation: In Hind Swaraj (1909), Chapter 10 ("The Condition of India: The Hindus and the Mahomedans"), Mahatma Gandhi argued for an inclusive concept of Indian nationhood, stating that India has historically assimilated diverse populations and that "The introduction of foreigners does not necessarily destroy the nation, they merge in it."

items.title: Mock #04 · Q41
items.stem:
Match List | with List II

|Terms Theorists

JA. arche-ecriture |, Julia Kristeva

B. cyborg I. Donna Haraway

IC. genotext Il. Friedrich Schleiermacher
Choose the correct answer from the options given below
items.explanation: Jacques Derrida introduced 'archi-écriture' (arche-writing) in Of Grammatology (1967), and feminist theorist Donna Haraway formulated the 'cyborg' in 'A Cyborg Manifesto' (1985). Julia Kristeva distinguished 'genotext' and 'phenotext' in Revolution in Poetic Language (1974), and German theologian Friedrich Schleiermacher developed the 'hermeneutic circle'.

items.title: Mock #04 · Q42
items.stem:
Works like The Earthly Paradise, Dante and His Circle, Goblin Market and Other Poems
and the journal, The Germ are associated with ________
items.explanation: All four items belong to the Pre-Raphaelite movement: William Morris's poem The Earthly Paradise (1868–1870), Dante Gabriel Rossetti's translations Dante and His Circle (1861/1874), Christina Rossetti's Goblin Market and Other Poems (1862), and the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood's short-lived periodical The Germ (1850).

items.title: Mock #04 · Q43
items.stem:
Pick out the two relevant and correct descriptions of U.R. Ananthamurthy's Samskara.
(1) The novel is written in English
(2) The novel is concerned with the progressive ideas of the times.
(3) The novel is set in Malgudi
(4) The novel is a satire on the representatives of a decadent Brahmin society.
(5) Samskara is a regional novel
(6) Praneschacharya does not atone for his sin.
items.explanation: Originally written in Kannada (1965) and translated into English by A.K. Ramanujan, U.R. Ananthamurthy's Samskara is a regional novel set in an orthodox agrahara (5) that critiques the hypocrisy and spiritual decay of a decadent Brahmin community (4).

items.title: Mock #04 · Q44
items.stem:
Which of the following characters in Moby Dick falls overboard and turns insane as a
result ?
items.explanation: In Chapter 93 ('The Castaway') of Herman Melville's Moby-Dick (1851), the young Black cabin boy Pip leaps from a whaleboat a second time, is left adrift in the vast ocean for hours, and loses his sanity from the terrifying isolation.

items.title: Mock #04 · Q45
items.stem:
Arrange the publication of the following books in chronological order.

A. The Location of Culture
B. The Future of the Race
C. Black Literature and Literary Theory
D. The Signifying Monkey: A Theory of Afro-American Literary Criticism
E. Reconstructing Womanhood: The Emergence of the Afro-American Woman Novelist

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, C, D, B and E
C, E, D, A and B
D, E, B, A and C
E, C, B, A and D
items.explanation: These critical texts were published chronologically as: Henry Louis Gates Jr.'s Black Literature and Literary Theory (1984, C), Hazel Carby's Reconstructing Womanhood (1987, E), Gates's The Signifying Monkey (1988, D), Homi Bhabha's The Location of Culture (1994, A), and Gates & West's The Future of the Race (1996, B).

items.title: Mock #04 · Q46
items.stem:
William Cowper rote in The Task (IV. 681-82) about those ho “Build factories ith blood,
conducting trade/At the sword’s point ...” These lines allude to :
options: West Indian slave-plantation owners and the East India Company ‘nabobs’
Exploiters of child labour in the ondon suburbs
items.explanation: In Book IV of The Task (1785), William Cowper condemns imperial greed and colonial exploitation, specifically excoriating the sugar plantation slaveholders of the West Indies and the corrupt, predatory 'nabobs' of the British East India Company.

items.title: Mock #04 · Q48
items.stem: Direct Method in English Language Teaching is also known as
items.explanation: In English language teaching, the Direct Method is commonly known as the Natural Method because it imitates first-language acquisition, immersing students directly in the target language through oral interaction and demonstration without translating into the mother tongue.

items.title: Mock #04 · Q49
items.stem:
The second part of Pilgrim's Progress deals with the pilgrimage of Christian's wife, Christiana.
She has a companion and a guide in this journey. Pick out the pair's names from the following
list.
(a)
Patience
(b)
Tenderheart

Mercy

items.title: Mock #04 · Q91

Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow:

"They define virtue to be life ordered according to nature, and that we be made by God for that end; but that nature doth allure and provoke us to a joy of life, that is to say to pleasure, as to the end of all our operations. But they think that not in every pleasure, but only in that which is good and honest, the felicity of man consisteth. For to virtue, say they, our nature is led by happiness, as to the chief and highest good. But of all pleasures they reckon those to be the chief which are seated in the mind, whereof the contemplation of virtue and the consciousness of a good life are the greatest. For bodily pleasure they think is to be desired only for health's sake, and that pain is the bitter enemy of pleasure."
— Thomas More, Utopia (Book II)

Question:

items.explanation: In Thomas More's Utopia (Book II), the passage explicitly declares that 'pain is the bitter enemy of pleasure', explaining why Utopians prize mental and moral virtues over fleeting bodily indulgences.

Question:
What does the first line of the passage say about external stimulus ?
options: External stimulus is irrelevant to the experience of health
External stimulus is the by-product of health
External stimulus is necessary condition for the experience of health
items.explanation: The opening sentence explains that 'nature doth allure and provoke us to a joy of life', indicating that external natural stimuli and provocations are necessary conditions that lead and awaken humanity to the experience of health and pleasure.

items.title: Mock #04 · Q96
items.meta: Unit IV / Unit VIII: Prose & Criticism
items.stem:
[Reading Comprehension: Poem]
Read the following poem carefully and answer the questions that follow:

"Between my finger and my thumb
The squat pen rests; snug as a gun.
Under my window, a clean rasping sound
When the spade sinks into gravelly ground:
My father, digging. I look down
Till his straining rump among the flowerbeds
Bends low, comes up twenty years away
Stooping in rhythm through potato drills
Where he was digging.
The coarse boot nestled on the lug, the shaft
Against the inside knee was levered firmly.
He rooted out tall tops, buried the bright edge deep
To scatter new potatoes that we picked,
Loving their cool hardness in our hands.
By God, the old man could handle a spade.
Just like his old man.
My grandfather cut more turf in a day
Than any other man on Toner's bog.
Once I carried him milk in a bottle
Corked sloppily with paper. He straightened up
To drink it, then fell to right away
Nicking and slicing neatly, heaving sods
Over his shoulder, going down and down
For the good turf. Digging.
The cold smell of potato mould, the squelch and slap
Of soggy peat, the curt cuts of an edge
Through living roots awaken in my head.
But I've no spade to follow men like them.
Between my finger and my thumb
The squat pen rests.
I'll dig with it."
— Seamus Heaney, "Digging" 

Question:
The comparison of gun to a pen in the poem signifies :
options: the power of written word to bring about change
the high administration of the speaker about father’s ability to use both pen and spade
that the act of writing can be as lethal as using a weapon
items.explanation: In the opening stanza of Seamus Heaney's 'Digging', the simile comparing the pen to a gun ('snug as a gun') suggests that the writer's craft can wield decisive agency, deadly precision, and power comparable to a weapon.
